# 17. Final Execution Roadmap — Master Document

**Document Version:** 1.0
**Date Generated:** 2026-08-05
**Generated By:** Technical Program Manager (Master Execution Roadmap)
**SRS Reference:** `docs/FathersNet-Complete-SRS.md` (FN-SRS-001 v2.0)
**Status:** Approved for Execution (pending Phase 0 decision approvals M-01…M-07)

**Purpose:** This is the **master execution roadmap** that ties every planning artifact into a single, executable sequence: requirement inventory (`00`), dependency map (`02`), architecture (`03`), technology stack (`04`), database (`05`), build plans (`06`–`10`), security (`11`), DevOps (`12`), testing (`13`), the phase roadmap (`14`), and the SRS quality gates (§17 QR), operations (§18 OR), disaster recovery (§19), and reference roadmap (Appendix D). It adds nothing new to the requirement set; it is the controlling sequencing, approval, cadence, escalation, critical-path, rollout, and handoff contract for execution.

**Classification convention:** **Confirmed** (SRS-stated / plan-stated) · **Recommended** (engineering decision) · **Configurable** (parameter with default) · **Assumption** (requires human validation). Every section carries a Source / Confidence / Reasoning / Impact-if-changed annotation.

---

## 1. Executive Purpose

FathersNet (Ayay) is a greenfield build — the repository contains documentation only (`version.md`: "SRS-only documentation repository; greenfield implementation; no application source code exists"). The SRS freezes 349 requirements (`00-requirement-inventory.md`): 170 FR, 50 NFR, 40 AR, 30 OR, 19 QR, 20 US, 5 UC, 4 UR, plus 11 PD. The dependency map (`02` §3) establishes a mandatory build layering: *Infrastructure → Database → Authentication → User/Profile → Content/KB → Pregnancy Engine → WhatsApp → AI/RAG → Mobile → Admin → Research → Pilot Operations*. The phase roadmap (`14`) decomposes that layering into eleven verifiable phases (Phase 0–Phase 10) governed by three quality gates — **G1 (Planning & Architecture)**, **G2 (Core Platform & Security)**, **G3 (Release & Pilot Launch)** — with milestones **M0–M9**.

This roadmap's job is to make execution deterministic: it fixes the exact order of every work package (§3), the hard prerequisites (§4), the milestone/exit definitions (§5), every human approval that must occur before build work unlocks (§6), what evidence is verified at each milestone (§7), the operating rhythm (§8), the blocker path (§9), where delays will concentrate and how buffers are managed (§10), how the product reaches users (pilot → regional → national, §11), the explicit handoff to the implementation agent (§12), the execution risks (§13), and the verification method that proves each step (§14).

> **Source:** FN-SRS-001 v2.0; `00`; `02`; `14`; `version.md`.
> **Confidence:** High — every number and sequence below traces to a named section of `14` or the SRS; no requirement was added or dropped.
> **Reasoning:** Execution quality on a 349-requirement, health-adjacent, multi-channel platform depends on ordering and evidence discipline more than on any single component; the SRS/`14` already mandate this layering and these gates.
> **Impact if changed:** If any phase is reordered or a gate is waived, the downstream "blockers if absent" of `02` §4 materialize (ungrounded AI, unapproved content, duplicate messages, data exposure), and QR-013 cannot be proven at pilot launch.

---

## 2. How to Use This Roadmap

### 2.1 Prerequisites (must be true before the first build task)

1. **Approve decision-log entries M-01…M-07** (`02` §6). These are the seven open decisions (cloud provider, WhatsApp provider, LLM provider, mobile framework, pilot cohort size, object storage + host, budget cap default). All are **Assumption-class** and require human validation. Note: `decision-log.md` is listed in the plan document set (`version.md`) but **is not yet authored** — its creation is the first execution artifact (WP-002, Phase 0). No code work may begin until all seven entries are recorded with an approver, rationale (ADR reference), and status **closed**.
2. **Read before executing (in this order):** `00-requirement-inventory.md` (what exists, 349 requirements) → `02-srs-requirement-analysis.md` (the dependency map that fixes build order) → `03-system-architecture-plan.md` (the target topology) → `14-development-phase-roadmap.md` (the phase/gate/milestone contract) → this document (the execution contract). `04` (stack), `05`–`13` (build plans) are read when each phase's work packages begin.
3. **Acknowledge document-set gaps.** Per the current repository, plan documents `15`–`23` (team/resource, risk, verification, handoff, resource/delivery, quality-gate checklist, feature matrix, healthcare compliance), `implementation-status.md`, and `decision-log.md` are **planned but not yet authored**. Until authored, their governing content is carried directly by `14` and the SRS. In particular, `21-quality-gate-checklist.md` **does not exist yet**; therefore gates **G1/G2/G3** are defined per `14` §1 (see §5 and §14 below). This gap is tracked as execution risk R-15 (§13).
4. **Role awareness:** Program Leadership and Security own gates; Backend/QA own phase evidence; the Medical Director (Program Champion) owns clinical content approval (QR-019/OR-021); the Research Lead owns ethics and research governance (OR-017); the Technical Lead owns work-package sequencing within a phase.

### 2.2 Reading rules

- This document is **not a requirement source**; it is a sequencing and control source. Where this document and `14` disagree, `14` and the SRS win.
- Work packages are atomic units of delivery (WP-001…WP-120, §3). A work package is **done** only when its named evidence artifact exists and is attached to the milestone record (§7).
- Any deviation (scope, order, gate, approval) requires a decision-log entry with an approver; silent deviation is a process violation.

> **Source:** `02` §6; `14` §1, §15; `version.md`; repository state.
> **Confidence:** High for the prerequisite list (each maps to a named SRS/plan item); the gap that `decision-log.md` and `15`–`23` are un-authored is a verified directory fact.
> **Reasoning:** The SRS treats decisions, consent, audit, encryption, and observability as never-retrofitted; forcing the seven decisions before code is the only way to honor that.
> **Impact if changed:** Executing before M-01…M-07 close risks provider lock-in, stack re-architecture (ADR churn), and procurement stalls (R-06, §13); executing without reading `00`/`02`/`03` invites requirement mis-scoping.

## 3. Exact Implementation Order

Numbered, sequential list of every work package in dependency order, derived from the dependency map in `02` §3 and the phase deliverables in `14` §3–§13. **The sequencing rule of `14` §14 applies: a phase may not begin its core build until the phase it depends on has its acceptance criteria met; overlap is permitted only off the critical path** (e.g., Phase 5 AI preparation may begin against content-service mocks while Phase 4 completes, but AI grounding requires the Phase 2 content service).

Legend — owner doc reference: **03** system architecture · **04** technology stack · **05** database · **06** backend · **07** WhatsApp · **08** AI/RAG · **09** mobile · **10** admin · **11** security/privacy · **12** DevOps/infra · **13** testing/quality · **14** phase roadmap · **15** team/resource · **16** risk · **19** handoff · **20** resource/delivery · **21** quality-gate checklist · **22** feature matrix · **23** healthcare compliance. Owners marked *planned (not yet authored)* are controlled by `14`/SRS until written.

## 4. Dependencies

### 4.1 Formal phase dependencies (hard prerequisites)

Per `02` §4 ("Blockers If Absent") and `14` §14 (cross-phase dependencies). A phase may not begin its core build until the prerequisite phase's acceptance criteria are evidenced.

| Phase | Hard Prerequisite Phases | Unlocks When Met | Blockers If Absent |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Phase 0 — Planning & Architecture Validation | None (SRS approved; M-01…M-07 require human validation) | All build phases | Unresolved decisions block every build decision |
| Phase 1 — Foundation | Phase 0 | All deploys from Phase 2 on | Nothing can run without IaC/secrets/CI/DB baseline |
| Phase 2 — Backend Core | Phase 1 (Gate G1) | Identity, enrollment, content, journeys | No persistence/identity → every service blocked |
| Phase 3 — Auth & Security | Phase 2 | WhatsApp, AI, mobile, admin, research consumption | Data exposure; Gate G2 failure blocks QR-013 |
| Phase 4 — WhatsApp | Phase 3 (Gate G2) + Phase 2 services | Primary conversational channel | No channel; no engagement engine |
| Phase 5 — AI/RAG | Phase 4 + Phase 2 content service | Grounded AI on both channels | Ungrounded answers; eval-set debt |
| Phase 6 — Mobile | Phase 3 + Phase 5 (AI endpoints) + Phase 4 parity | App surface | No mobile channel for non-WhatsApp fathers |
| Phase 7 — Admin | Phase 3 + Phases 2–5 services | Operational control | No way to operate/review/report |
| Phase 8 — Integration | Phases 4–7 all present + Phase 3 | Evidence generation; E2E flows; phased rollout | No research data; feature flags absent |
| Phase 9 — Testing | Phases 0–8 artifacts | Proven quality; Gate 3 evidence | Launching with unknown quality |
| Phase 10 — Pilot Deployment | Phase 9 (all gates green) | Live founding cohort | Cannot launch safely |

### 4.2 External dependencies (from SRS §1.9; all Confirmed unless marked)

| ID | Dependency | Where It Bites | Mitigation if Delayed |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| D-01 | WhatsApp Business API availability + policy acceptance in Ethiopia | Phase 0 procurement; Phase 4 (WP-033/038); Phase 10 launch | Provider abstraction (FR-149/AR-004) lets a secondary provider step in; Phase 3 webhook pattern is provider-agnostic (R-02) |
| D-02 | LLM/embedding provider availability, cost, compliance | Phase 0 (M-03); Phase 5 (WP-045/050/055) | Multi-provider fallback tiers (§9.8); cost-aware routing; DPAs in place (R-03) |
| D-03 | Cloud platform regional availability | Phase 0 (WP-006); Phase 1 (WP-010) | Single-cloud multi-zone readiness (ADR-006); verify region/zone availability before commit |
| D-04 | Clinical/medical review of content and AI responses | Phase 2 (WP-020); Phase 5 (WP-045); Phase 9 (WP-108) | Content team runs ahead of Phase 2; review workflow built in Phase 2; QR-019 scheduled early in Phase 9 (R-04) |
| D-05 | Research ethics approval | Phase 0 (WP-007); Phase 8 (WP-087); Phase 10 (WP-119) | Research consent model designed in Phase 0; pipeline built behind feature flags in Phase 8; governance gates pre-approved (R-05) |
| D-06 | Voice transcription/translation for EN/AM | Phase 4 (WP-039); Phase 5 voice | Primary + fallback transcription providers (AssemblyAI primary / Google fallback) |

### 4.3 Configurable assumptions that gate procurement

M-01 cloud provider (ADR-006), M-02 WhatsApp provider, M-03 LLM provider contract + DPA, M-04 mobile framework, M-05 pilot cohort size (default 500+), M-06 object storage + host, M-07 budget cap default (SRS §5.9, §8.3). All are **Assumption-class**: each must be resolved by a named human approver in the decision log before its consuming phase starts (`02` §6).

### 4.4 Sequencing rule (Confirmed)

"a phase may not begin its core build until the phase it depends on (02 §4) has its acceptance criteria met. Overlap is permitted only for phases that are not on the critical dependency path (e.g., Phase 5 AI preparation can begin against content-service mocks while Phase 4 completes, but AI grounding against real knowledge requires Phase 2 content service)." (`14` §14)

> **Source:** `02` §4; `14` §14; SRS §1.9 (A/D/C tables).
> **Confidence:** High — the phase→prerequisite matrix is lifted directly from `14` §2.1 and `02` §4; external dependencies are the SRS D-01…D-06 list.
> **Reasoning:** Dependencies here are formal (hard), not advisory; the SRS labels them **Confirmed**.
> **Impact if changed:** Weakening any hard prerequisite converts a design-time constraint into an operational incident (e.g., shipping WhatsApp without HMAC webhook pattern = forged-message risk; shipping AI without eval set = unmeasured hallucination risk in a live pilot).

| **M1 — Foundation live** | End of Phase 1: reproducible, secure delivery platform | Gate 1 acceptance: IaC applies cleanly; CI/CD gates block promotion; migration 001 run/rollback; zero secrets; observability + synthetic alert | **Gate G1 accepted** | §4, §15 |

| **M4 — Channels integrated** | End of Phase 5: WhatsApp ↔ AI RAG E2E | Provider-switch test; state-machine matrix; emergency drills EN/AM; media pipeline; QR-010 + QR-011 pass; AI eval set + safety regression pass | Internal checkpoint | §7–§8, §15 |
| **M5 — App + Admin feature complete** | End of Phases 6–7: mobile + admin surfaces | Mobile E2E journeys (offline sync, emergency cache, Amharic, assistive tech ≥ 80%); admin role tests; MFA; WCAG 2.1 AA | Internal checkpoint | §9–§10, §15 |
| **M6 — Integration complete** | End of Phase 8: research pipeline, partner sync, feature flags, E2E data flows | UC-001…UC-005 E2E pass; research records anonymized + themes; governed export audited; partner sync conflict-merge; notification failover; canary/rollback | Internal checkpoint | §11, §15 |
| **M7 — QA + UAT complete** | End of Phase 9: full quality program executed | Gates 2–3 verified: all QR-001…QR-019; zero critical/high; performance targets; UAT sign-off (QR-017); clinical validation (QR-019); traceability 100% Must-Have | **Gates 2–3 verified** | §12, §15 |
| **M8 — Pilot go-live** | Start of Phase 10: founding cohort onboarding begins | **Gate 3 granted**: QR-013 evidence; rollback readiness (QR-016); monitoring/alerting live; DR drill met | **Gate G3 granted** | §13, §15 |

> **Source:** `14` §15 (milestone table) and `14` §3–§13 (per-phase exit criteria).
> **Confidence:** High — definitions and exit criteria are the `14` milestone table verbatim in substance.
> **Reasoning:** Milestones are evidence-bound so that "done" is verifiable, consistent with QR-013/QR-015 discipline.
> **Impact if changed:** Renaming/relocating a milestone or softening an exit criterion weakens the gate chain G1→G2→G3 that QR-013 depends on.

> **Reasoning:** Health-adjacent, research-bearing platforms fail on missed human gates, not missed code; approvals are the control points where program, clinical, ethics, security, and operations become accountable.
> **Impact if changed:** Skipping any approval converts a designed-in control into a compliance/patient-safety finding at the worst possible moment (QR-013 gate or during live pilot).

| M7 | Quality + UAT complete | Per-layer test execution reports; pen-test report; load-test report; accessibility audit; UAT sign-off records; clinical-validation sign-off; traceability matrix export; Gates 2–3 checklist signed | `13` QR-001…QR-019 sweep; SRS §18.3 alert verification |
| M8 | Pilot go-live | Gate 3 sign-off; enrollment/onboarding reports; support-SLA metrics; monitoring dashboard + alert captures; DR drill report (RPO/RTO measurements); rollback drill log | `13` QR-016/QR-017/QR-019; SRS §18.1–§18.4 live operations |
| M9 | Pilot evaluated | QR-018 pilot-evaluation report with KPI dashboard export (PD-004…PD-008, FR-118, Appendix F); post-incident review records; safety-event review (zero critical follow-through failures) | `13` QR-018; SRS §18.5 maintenance + OR-018 M&E |

**Evidence repository rule:** every artifact named above is stored per phase so a reviewer can audit any acceptance criterion end-to-end (artifact repository, §14.7). Evidence is produced continuously during each phase, never reconstructed at gate time.

| Quarterly impact report | Quarterly | Program KPIs, research findings, cost per enrolled father | Research Lead |
| On-call rotation | Continuous during pilot | OR-001 on-call coverage; severity-based response (§9) | Operations |
| Incident post-incident reviews | After each Sev1/Sev2 incident | OR-009: detection→triage→containment→resolution→PIR→action tracking | Operations + Security |

**Delivery cadence rule:** a sprint is complete when its assigned work packages have their named evidence artifacts recorded (§7); demos and retros do not replace acceptance evidence.

> **Reasoning:** A health-adjacent pilot needs both delivery rhythm and an evidence rhythm; the two must not diverge.

## 9. Escalation Path

### 9.1 Blocked work-package escalation

| Level | Trigger | Action | Target Response |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 — Team | WP blocked > 1 day; prerequisite missing | Record blocker in tracker; find workaround or re-sequence within phase (off critical path) | Same day |
| 1 — Phase | Phase-exit criteria unmet; gate evidence missing | Hold phase-exit; escalate to Program Manager; add recovery plan | 2 days |
| 2 — Program | Gate G1/G2/G3 hold; decision M-01…M-07 undecided; scope conflict | Decision-log entry + Program Leadership review; risk-accepted only by named approver | 1 week (or decision deadline) |
| 3 — Leadership | External blocker (D-01…D-06); funding; regulatory | Program Champion / MERQ Leadership; invoke contingency (provider abstraction, alternate supplier) | 2 weeks |

### 9.2 Support and incident escalation (SRS §18.4, OR-009)

| Level | Channel | Scope | Handling |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| L1 | AI assistant + self-service | Common questions, FAQ | Automated; monitored |
| L2 | Support team | Account, consent, troubleshooting | SLA-defined response (OR-002) |
| L3 | Technical engineering | System bugs, L2 escalations | Runbook-driven; severity-based |
| L4 | Emergency healthcare escalation | Danger-sign handling → facility care + on-call reviewer | Immediate; 5-min follow-up (WP-040); admin alert |

**Severity model (Confirmed, SRS §18.3/OR-008):** Sev1 — service down or emergency-escalation failure (on-call paged immediately); Sev2 — high error rate, security event, queue backlog (priority alert); Sev3 — degraded feature (standard alert); Sev4 — cosmetic/non-urgent (ticket). Emergency-escalation failures are always Sev1 and are the highest-priority alert class (§18.3).

### 9.3 Rule for gates

A gate is never unilaterally waived. If a gate cannot be met, the Program Leadership decides explicitly between (a) extend schedule, (b) reduce scope via decision log (Could-Have items only), or (c) risk-accept with a named approver and a remediation plan. Silent continuation past a gate is a process violation (§2.2).

> **Source:** SRS §18.3, §18.4; OR-008, OR-009, OR-002, OR-003; `14` §15; `16`* (risk register baseline).
> **Confidence:** High — levels, severity classes, and the no-waive rule trace to SRS §18 and `14` gates.
> **Reasoning:** Blockers are predictable on a provider-laden health platform; a pre-agreed path keeps decisions fast and documented.
> **Impact if changed:** A missing escalation path converts a 2-day blocker into a multi-week stall or an unlogged risk-acceptance.

## 10. Critical Path Analysis

### 10.1 The longest chain

The mandatory chain (from `02` §3 and `14` §2.1): **Phase 0 → 1 → 2 → 3 → 4 → 5 → 8 → 9 → 10**. Phases 6 (Mobile) and 7 (Admin) are off the critical path — they depend on Phase 5 (AI endpoints / services) and feed Phase 8 (Integration), so they may run parallel to Phase 5's tail but must complete before Phase 8 starts. Phase 8 is on the critical path because research/analytics, feature-flag rollout, and E2E data flows gate the QA sweep and pilot.

Critical-chain effort at **realistic** reference values (`14` §16.1): P0 16 + P1 26 + P2 62 + P3 36 + P4 40 + P5 46 + P8 20 + P9 42 + P10 26 = **314 person-weeks**; total program reference 404 person-weeks (the difference is the parallel P6 56 + P7 34 + buffers). At a steady-state ~10–12 FTE team, the realistic calendar outcome is **~42 weeks** (best ~32 / conservative ~58; `14` §16.2). All figures are configurable references, not commitments.

### 10.2 Where delays concentrate

| Concentration Point | Why | Effect on Critical Path | Mitigation / Buffer |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Phase 0 decisions M-01…M-07 (A-01…A-07) | Human-validation class; procurement lead times | Blocks every downstream build decision | Decision log is a Phase 0 hard exit; parallel supplier negotiations; fallback options pre-qualified (R-06) |
| Provider onboarding D-01…D-03, D-06 | WhatsApp policy/availability, LLM DPAs, transcription readiness | Hits P4/P5 start | Procurement in Phase 0 (WP-006); provider abstraction from day one; transcription primary + fallback |
| Clinical review throughput D-04 | Backlog risk (R-04) | Hits WP-020 (content), WP-038 (templates), WP-045 (ingestion), WP-108 (QR-019) | Content team runs ahead of Phase 2; review workflow built in Phase 2; QR-019 scheduled early in Phase 9 |
| Ethics approval D-05 | Board timelines | Hits Phase 8 research activation (WP-087) and pilot evaluation | Consent model + approval plan designed in Phase 0 (WP-007); pipeline behind feature flags |
| AI eval set + safety regression (WP-056) | Ground-truth annotation effort; quality bar ≥ 90% | Hits Phase 9 and any AI release | Eval set started with the safety layer, not deferred to Phase 9 (R-11) |
| Phase 9 full QA sweep | 16-layer test program; pen-test + UAT scheduling | Directly precedes Gate 3 | Test pyramids shipped per phase (`14` §2.3); no phase defers its own tests (R-01) |

### 10.3 Buffer strategy

1. **Schedule buffer:** ~15% of calendar time held at the program level (not consumed by scope creep; released only by decision-log approval).
2. **Overlap off critical path:** Phase 5 AI prep against content-service mocks while Phase 4 completes; Phase 6/7 parallel to Phase 5 tail — permitted by `14` §14; critical-path dependencies are never parallelized.
3. **Parallel supplier work:** all three provider tracks (cloud, WhatsApp, LLM/ASR) negotiated in Phase 0 with fallbacks, so D-01…D-03/D-06 never hold a start.
4. **Evidence flowing, not gated:** each phase ships its own tests and traceability so gates are provable at each step rather than reconstructed at the end (`14` §2.3, §18).
5. **Content/clinical head start:** the content team begins authoring against the authoritative guide before Phase 2 completes, decoupling D-04 from the build.

> **Source:** `02` §3–§4; `14` §2.1, §14, §16; `20`* (resource/delivery analysis, planned).
> **Confidence:** Medium-High — the critical chain follows the mandatory dependency map (High); calendar figures are configurable references (Medium).
> **Reasoning:** The dependency map is explicitly sequential; the only degrees of freedom are off-path overlap and buffer placement, both of which `14` already constrains.
> **Impact if changed:** Parallelizing a critical-path dependency (e.g., starting Phase 5 AI against the real KB before WP-020 content approval) reintroduces the ungrounded-AI blocker; consuming buffers without decision-log approval silently re-creates R-01.

## 11. Rollout Plan

### 11.1 Phased rollout model (OR-027: pilot → regional → national)

Rollout is controlled by **feature flags (FR-168)** and **wave gates**. A wave is a controlled expansion of the founding cohort, not a code release — code releases are continuous and canary-rolled (WP-092, SRS §16.2); user exposure grows in waves.

| Wave | Scope | Entry Condition (Gate) | Feature-Flag Profile | Exit / Evaluation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Wave 0 — Internal alpha** | MERQ staff/dev team; no external fathers | Phase 9 UAT (QR-017) + clinical validation (QR-019) | Full MVP feature set, all flags ON for testers; emergency drill exercised | UAT sign-off; defects triaged |
| **Wave 1 — Founding-cohort pilot** | Founding cohort per M-05 (default 500+); Ethiopia, EN/AM | **Gate G3 granted** (M8) | MVP set ON: WhatsApp enrollment, prompts/pulses/legacy, pregnancy journey, AI assistant, journal, checklists/budget, reminders, research collection, admin | **QR-018 pilot evaluation** (M9): PD-004…PD-008 + Appendix F KPIs; safety review |
| **Wave 2 — Expanded cohort / regional** | Growth toward thousands; additional regions within Ethiopia | Wave 1 evaluation meets KPI thresholds; zero critical/high; capacity review (NFR-001…NFR-009) | Additional flags ON as evaluated: campaigns at scale, partner sync, pre/post assessment, AI ops dashboards, mobile distribution (Play Store) | Regional M&E report |
| **Wave 3 — National expansion** | National scale; content/translation/clinical load reviewed | Wave 2 KPIs + infrastructure cost model reviewed (`20`*) | Full feature set incl. could-do backlog items (WP-120) | National impact report |
| **Wave 4 — Regional (East Africa)** | Deferred per SRS §2.8.2 (multi-country) | Separate program decision; additional languages, ethics, legal (NFR-041) | New localization/consent/regulatory flags | Board decision |

### 11.2 Feature-flag candidates (FR-168)

Rollout is exercised through named flags, each toggled per wave and canary-deployed with rollback: `ai_assistant`, `medical_safety_layer` (never off in production), `research_pipeline`, `partner_sync`, `campaign_engine`, `sms_fallback`, `pre_post_assessment`, `mobile_offline_sync`, `admin_ai_ops`, `play_store_distribution`, `myth_classification`. **Safety controls (emergency workflow, safety layer, opt-in/opt-out enforcement) are not feature-flag-disabled in any wave** — they are baseline platform invariants.

### 11.3 Wave-planning rules

1. Each wave has a written entry brief (scope, flags, capacity, support staffing, KPIs) approved by Program Leadership.
2. A wave does not expand until the prior wave's evaluation metrics are reviewed (PD-004…PD-008, Appendix F).
3. Rollback at any wave = revert flags (FR-168), roll back versioned content/app releases (OR-030), and stand down cohort expansion.

> **Source:** SRS §2.8.2, OR-027, OR-030, FR-168, Appendix J; `14` §11 (WP-092), §13.
> **Confidence:** High for the pilot→regional→national structure (OR-027 is Must-Have); Medium for wave thresholds (configurable targets).
> **Reasoning:** The SRS explicitly mandates phased rollout with feature flags; wave gates keep exposure commensurate with evidence.
> **Impact if changed:** Skipping wave gates (e.g., expanding before QR-018 evaluation) risks scaling engagement problems and unmeasured AI-safety incidents across a national cohort.

## 12. Handoff to Implementation Agent

### 12.1 Explicit next step

**The next step after this document is Phase 0 then Phase 1 execution, per `14` (Development Phase Roadmap) and `19` (Engineering Handoff Package).** Because `19-engineering-handoff-package.md` is not yet authored, the implementation agent's controlling execution references for the first two phases are **`14` §3–§4, this document §3 (WP-001…WP-014), `02` §6, `03`, `04`, and `05`**.

### 12.2 Required reading order before any code

1. `00-requirement-inventory.md` — the 349-requirement baseline.
2. `02-srs-requirement-analysis.md` — the dependency map (§3) and the seven decisions M-01…M-07 (§6).
3. `03-system-architecture-plan.md` — the target topology the foundation must reproduce.
4. `04-technology-stack-analysis.md` — stack to sign off.
5. `05-database-implementation-plan.md` — migration-001 scope.
6. `14-development-phase-roadmap.md` — phase contract, gates, acceptance criteria.
7. This document — ordering, gates, approvals, cadence, escalation, critical path, rollout.

### 12.3 Non-negotiable execution guardrails

1. **No application code before Phase 0 artifacts are signed** (decision log M-01…M-07, architecture review, stack sign-off, STRIDE, DPIA). Foundation tooling (repo, CI skeleton, IaC) may begin only after WP-001…WP-005 are evidenced.
2. **Create and close `decision-log.md` (WP-002) before any provider-dependent build.** Record M-01…M-07 with approver + ADR reference; statuses closed.
3. **Cross-cutting controls are never retrofitted** (`02` §5): security/privacy, auditability, localization (EN/AM from first string), observability, idempotency, testing discipline apply from Phase 1.
4. **No production data in lower environments** (AR-009); secrets only via the secret manager (NFR-022).
5. **A phase is done only when its named evidence artifacts (§7) are recorded**; update traceability at every milestone (QR-015).
6. **Gate discipline:** do not begin Phase 2 until Gate G1 is accepted; do not begin Phase 4 until Gate G2 is accepted; do not onboard the founding cohort until Gate G3 is granted.
7. **Escalate, don't stall:** use §9; a decision-log entry accompanies every deviation.

### 12.4 First 10 actions for the implementation agent

1. Read §12.2 documents.
2. Freeze SRS baseline + stand up traceability framework (WP-001).
3. Create decision log; drive M-01…M-07 to closure with named approvers (WP-002).
4. Run architecture review + stack sign-off (WP-003, WP-004).
5. Produce STRIDE + DPIA (WP-005).
6. Kick off procurement incl. WhatsApp Business Manager + LLM/ASR + cloud + object storage (WP-006).
7. Stand up research ethics groundwork (WP-007).
8. Assemble Gate G1 package; begin Phase 1 Foundation (WP-008…WP-014).
9. Prove CI/CD → IaC → secrets → migration 001 → observability; capture Gate 1 evidence.
10. Hold phase-exit review; request Gate G1 acceptance before Phase 2.

> **Source:** `14` §1, §3–§4; `19`* (planned); `02` §6; repository state.
> **Confidence:** High for the guardrails (each is a confirmed SRS/`14` rule); the reading order and first-10-actions are derived directly from WP-001…WP-014.
> **Reasoning:** The program is greenfield; the handoff must make the sequence self-starting while keeping the human gates in front of the code.
> **Impact if changed:** An agent that starts coding before WP-001…WP-007 violates the no-retrofit rule and risks the exact R-06/R-08 failures the plan exists to prevent.

## 14. Verification Approach

This roadmap is itself verified, not just executed. The method mirrors `14` §18 and the SRS quality framework, and serves as the master checkpoint method until `21` and `18-implementation-verification-plan.md` are authored.

1. **Traceability as the spine (QR-015).** Every phase deliverable maps to named requirements via `00`/`22`*. The traceability matrix is refreshed at every milestone and must show 100% of Must-Have requirements covered with test/verification status before Gate G3. WP-106 is the Phase 9 refresh; WP-001 stands the framework up.
2. **Quality-gate checklists (Gates G1/G2/G3).** Gates are defined in `14` §1: G1 (Planning & Architecture — accepted end of Phase 1), G2 (Core Platform & Security — accepted end of Phase 3), G3 (Release & Pilot Launch — granted at Phase 10). Until `21-quality-gate-checklist.md` is authored, the gate item lists are the acceptance criteria + verification-evidence sections of `14` §4/§6/§13 and the evidence table in §7 above. **A gate is not closed on narrative; it is closed on named evidence artifacts.**
3. **Test pyramids per phase (QR-001…QR-012).** Each phase ships unit, integration, and relevant E2E tests with coverage floors (QR-002). Full-system sweeps land in Phase 9: performance (QR-006), security (QR-007), accessibility (QR-008), privacy (QR-009), WhatsApp (QR-010), AI evaluation (QR-011), test data hygiene (QR-012) — executed as WPs 095–105.
4. **Release discipline (QR-013, QR-014, QR-016).** No production/pilot deployment without the combined release gate (unit+integration+E2E+security+accessibility+performance+clinical review), the AI eval set + safety regression for every AI release, and release review (rollback readiness, dashboards, alerting). Production promotion additionally requires the SRS §16.2 manual approval gate + canary health-check promotion.
5. **Human-in-the-loop gates (QR-017, QR-018, QR-019).** UAT with representative users, pilot evaluation against the KPI framework (PD-011, Appendix F), and clinical/content validation against the authoritative guide (A-04) are evidence-bearing checkpoints with sign-off records — approvals A-12, A-13, A-19.
6. **DR and operations proof (§19, OR-012).** RPO ≤ 15 min / RTO ≤ 4 h are demonstrated by scheduled restore/failover drills with measurements, not assumed; monitoring/alerting are verified live before cohort onboarding (WP-113, WP-116). Backup verification runs on schedule (NFR-014).
7. **Artifact repository.** All verification evidence (test reports, scans, drills, sign-offs, dashboards) is recorded per phase (WP evidence tables, §7) so a reviewer can audit any acceptance criterion end-to-end — the plan-wide evidence convention used across `06`–`13`.
8. **Status tracking.** A live `implementation-status.md` (planned; to be created in WP-001) records per-WP status, gate state, decision-log status, and open risks, so Program Leadership can read the entire execution state from one file.

> **Source:** `14` §18 (7-point method); SRS §17 (QR-001…QR-019), §19 (RPO/RTO); SRS §16.2 (deployment gates).
> **Confidence:** High — each numbered method traces to a named SRS/`14` control.
> **Reasoning:** Verification is only meaningful if it is continuous, evidence-bound, and auditable; the method makes every gate and milestone reproducible.
> **Impact if changed:** Reverting to narrative closure or deferred verification is exactly the failure QR-013 exists to prevent and would produce an un-auditable launch.
